newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing personal savings 175.7 bln yuan end-March.
newsitem.headline: Beijing personal savings 175.7 bln yuan end-March.

text.p: Individual savings in China's capital, Beijing, reached 175.7 billion yuan ($21.16 billion) at end-March, the Beijing Economic Daily said on Thursday.
That marked an increase of five billion yuan compared with the start of the year, but was 10.1 billion yuan less than the increase in the same period a year ago, it said.
It was the lowest rate of increase in four years, it said, quoting statistics from the Beijing branch of the central bank.

Of the total, 154.4 billion was held in time deposit accounts and 21.3 billion in current accounts. Time deposits accounted for 87.8 percent of the total but the amount was falling, the newspaper said.

The slow rate of increase was due to competition from issues of corporate bonds and treasury bonds and the bull run on China's two stock markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen that have attracted funds, the newspaper quoted a central bank official as saying.
In the first quarter alone, Beijing residents opened 81,000 new shareholder's accounts, 45,000 more than in the same period a year ago, he said.
